name: Muruntau Gold Mine
owner: Navoi Mining & Metallurgy Combinat (state-owned)
production: ~2.9 Moz/year — world's largest open-pit gold mine
strategic_value: Largest single gold source globally; Uzbekistan leverages output to diversify away from cotton dependency and build Central Asian influence

name: Grasberg Mine
owner: PT Freeport Indonesia (51% Indonesian govt, 49% Freeport-McMoRan)
production: ~1.8 Moz gold + ~1.4B lbs copper/year — world's largest gold reserve
strategic_value: Largest gold reserve by contained ounces; Indonesian state takeover from US firm reflects resource nationalism trend across Global South

name: Nevada Gold Mines
owner: Barrick Gold (61.5%) / Newmont (38.5%) joint venture
production: ~3.3 Moz/year combined — largest gold-producing complex in the world
strategic_value: Anchors Western gold supply chain; Nevada produces ~72% of all US gold; critical for dollar credibility and Fed reserve backing

name: Witwatersrand Basin
owner: Multiple operators (Harmony Gold, Sibanye-Stillwater, AngloGold Ashanti)
production: ~90 tonnes/year (declining) — produced ~50,000 tonnes historically, ~40% of all gold ever mined
strategic_value: Historically dominant gold province now in decline; deep-level mining increasingly uneconomical; South Africa's BRICS membership complicates alignment

name: Olimpiada Mine
owner: Polyus Gold (Russian, controlled by Said Kerimov)
production: ~1.5 Moz/year — Russia's largest gold mine
strategic_value: Backbone of Russia's domestic gold production; Polyus is world's 4th largest gold miner; fuels sanctions evasion via gold exports to UAE and Turkey
alert: Polyus subject to indirect Western sanctions; gold export routes under surveillance

name: Syama Gold Mine
owner: Resolute Mining (Australian) — under Malian junta pressure
production: ~200 koz/year
strategic_value: Mali junta backed by Wagner/Africa Corps detained Resolute CEO in Nov 2024 demanding renegotiation; part of pattern of resource nationalism enabled by Russian military presence
alert: Resolute CEO detained Nov 2024; Mali demanding larger state share under Wagner security umbrella

name: Loulo-Gounkoto Gold Complex
owner: Barrick Gold (80%) / Mali govt (20%)
production: ~510 koz/year — Mali's largest gold operation
strategic_value: Barrick's flagship African asset; Mali is Africa's 3rd largest gold producer; junta seeks to increase state share from 20% to 35% under new mining code
alert: Mali's 2023 mining code demands higher state equity; Barrick in tense negotiations with Wagner-backed junta

name: Hassai Gold Mine
owner: La Mancha Resources (linked to Naguib Sawiris) — previously Wagner-linked artisanal operations nearby
production: ~200 koz/year (industrial); artisanal gold estimated 50-80 tonnes/year from wider region
strategic_value: Sudan is Africa's 3rd largest gold producer; Wagner/Africa Corps documented smuggling artisanal gold via Khartoum and Port Sudan to fund RSF and Russian operations
alert: Active civil war zone; Wagner-linked gold smuggling documented by UN Panel of Experts; gold funds both sides of conflict

name: Essakane Gold Mine
owner: iamgold (Canadian, 90%) / Burkina Faso govt (10%)
production: ~370 koz/year — Burkina Faso's largest mine
strategic_value: Burkina Faso junta (post-2022 coup) invited Wagner/Africa Corps; new mining code demands 10% free carry + 5% paid participation; Western miners under pressure
alert: Military junta aligned with Russia; jihadist attacks near mining areas; Western operators face nationalization risk

name: Inata Gold Mine
owner: Previously Avocet Mining (collapsed); now under Burkina state review
production: Suspended — previously ~80 koz/year
strategic_value: Symbol of mining sector collapse in Sahel; 2021 massacre of soldiers guarding mine exposed state failure; Wagner presence now fills security vacuum
alert: Non-operational; site of 2021 Inata attack (53 soldiers killed); Wagner controls security perimeter

name: CAR Gold & Diamond Fields
owner: Artisanal miners under Wagner/Africa Corps control; Midas Resources (Wagner-linked)
production: ~2-3 tonnes gold/year (estimated); ~300k carats diamonds/year (artisanal)
strategic_value: Wagner's original African resource extraction model; gold and diamonds fund Africa Corps operations; CAR is testing ground for Russia's resource-for-security model across Africa
alert: UN-documented conflict resource extraction; Kimberley Process concerns; EU sanctions on Wagner-linked mining entities

name: Zijin Mining — Buritica Mine
owner: Zijin Mining Group (Chinese state-linked)
production: ~250 koz/year
strategic_value: Chinese mining footprint in Western Hemisphere; Zijin is China's largest gold miner with assets across 4 continents; Colombia asset gives Beijing resource leverage in US backyard

name: Zijin Mining — Kamoa-Kakula (Copper + Gold)
owner: Ivanhoe Mines (40%) / Zijin Mining (40%) / DRC govt (20%)
production: Primarily copper (~400 kt/year) with gold by-product; world-class Tier 1 mine
strategic_value: Chinese co-ownership of DRC's premier new mine; DRC minerals are critical to global energy transition; Beijing secures supply chain from mine to processing

name: Russia Central Bank Gold Reserve
owner: Central Bank of Russia
production: ~2,336 tonnes (as of 2024) — 5th largest globally; added ~300 tonnes since 2022 sanctions
strategic_value: Aggressive gold accumulation to sanctions-proof reserves after $300B in forex frozen; gold now ~30% of total reserves; enables yuan/rupee settlement bypassing dollar
alert: Russia banned from London gold market; trades gold via UAE, Turkey, China intermediaries

name: China PBOC Gold Reserve
owner: People's Bank of China
production: ~2,264 tonnes officially (as of 2024); actual holdings estimated 4,000-5,000 tonnes including undisclosed state reserves
strategic_value: 18 consecutive months of buying through mid-2024; de-dollarization strategy; gold backs potential future yuan internationalization or BRICS currency unit
alert: Actual gold holdings likely far exceed official figures; strategic opacity is deliberate

name: India RBI Gold Reserve
owner: Reserve Bank of India
production: ~854 tonnes (as of 2024) — up from 668 tonnes in 2020; aggressive buying since 2022
strategic_value: India diversifying reserves away from dollar; repatriated 100 tonnes from Bank of England in 2024; gold backs IMEC corridor financing and rupee settlement ambitions

name: Turkey CBRT Gold Reserve
owner: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
production: ~585 tonnes (as of 2024); Turkey also largest gold recycler in region
strategic_value: Erdogan uses gold to hedge lira instability; Turkey is key gold transit hub between Russia and global markets; Turkish refineries process sanctioned Russian gold
alert: Turkish refineries accused of laundering Russian-origin gold; LBMA watchlist concerns

name: Dubai Gold Souk — Russia/Africa Gold Route
owner: Multiple UAE refineries (Kaloti, Emirates Gold, Al Etihad)
production: UAE imports ~1,200 tonnes/year; re-exports ~800 tonnes; significant Russian and African artisanal gold flows through Dubai
strategic_value: World's largest physical gold trading hub; key node in sanctions evasion — Russian gold enters via Turkey/Central Asia, African conflict gold via Kampala/Khartoum; laundered into legitimate supply chain
alert: Multiple UAE refineries removed from LBMA Good Delivery List; Swiss imports of UAE gold flagged for Russian origin

name: Alrosa Diamond Mines
owner: Alrosa PJSC (33% Russian govt, 25% Sakha Republic)
production: ~30 million carats/year — ~27% of global rough diamond supply by volume
strategic_value: World's largest diamond producer by volume; Western sanctions since 2022 disrupted but didn't eliminate trade; diamonds rerouted via India, UAE, and Central Asia
alert: EU/US/G7 sanctions since 2022; Belgium's Antwerp banned direct imports Jan 2024; Indian cutting centers still process via third countries

name: De Beers — Jwaneng Mine
owner: Debswana (50% De Beers/Anglo American + 50% Botswana govt)
production: ~12 million carats/year — world's richest diamond mine by value
strategic_value: Single most valuable diamond mine on Earth; Botswana renegotiated deal in 2023 to receive larger share of rough diamonds for local beneficiation; power shifting from London to Gaborone
alert: 2023 Botswana-De Beers renegotiation shifts power; Botswana threatened to leave partnership if terms not improved

name: De Beers — Orapa & Letlhakane Mines
owner: Debswana (50% De Beers/Anglo American + 50% Botswana govt)
production: ~6 million carats/year combined
strategic_value: Botswana is world's 2nd largest diamond producer; diamonds are 70% of export revenue; new deal gives Botswana right to sell 30% of production independently

name: Catoca Diamond Mine
owner: Endiama (41%, Angolan state) / Alrosa (41%) / Odebrecht (18%)
production: ~6.8 million carats/year — world's 4th largest diamond mine
strategic_value: Alrosa's 41% stake gives Russia major foothold in African diamonds; Angola under pressure to divest Russian partner but resists; potential sanctions evasion vector
alert: Alrosa's stake makes this a sanctions compliance flashpoint; Angola resists Western pressure to force divestment

name: Marange Diamond Fields
owner: ZCDC (Zimbabwe Consolidated Diamond Company, state-owned)
production: ~3.5 million carats/year (estimated; actual figures opaque)
strategic_value: Military-controlled diamond fields with documented human rights abuses; Kimberley Process certification controversially maintained; Zimbabwe pivots toward China and Russia
alert: History of military violence against artisanal miners; revenues bypass treasury; Kimberley Process credibility test case

name: DRC Artisanal Diamond Fields
owner: Artisanal miners / MIBA (state, largely collapsed) / various armed groups
production: ~12-16 million carats/year (mostly industrial grade); significant smuggling to Congo-Brazzaville and Angola
strategic_value: DRC produces more diamonds by volume than any nation except Russia; almost entirely artisanal; funds armed groups in eastern DRC; child labor pervasive
alert: Ongoing armed conflict in eastern DRC; M23 rebel group (Rwanda-backed) controls some mining areas; supply chain traceability near zero

name: Sierra Leone — Koidu Mine
owner: Octea Mining (linked to Beny Steinmetz, Israeli billionaire) — license under dispute
production: ~300k carats/year (reduced); artisanal mining ~1M carats/year from alluvial deposits
strategic_value: Infamous 'blood diamond' origin; post-war recovery model; Chinese artisanal miners increasingly present; government seeking to formalize sector
alert: Ownership disputed; Steinmetz corruption cases in multiple jurisdictions; artisanal sector largely unregulated

name: Surat Diamond Processing Hub
owner: ~6,000 cutting/polishing units (private, family-owned businesses)
production: Processes ~90% of world's diamonds by volume; employs ~800,000 workers; $24B annual exports
strategic_value: India's diamond processing monopoly gives it enormous leverage in global supply chain; G7 Russian diamond ban requires India's cooperation to be effective; India resists full compliance
alert: G7 traceability requirements (Jan 2024) threaten Surat's role if Russian diamonds can't be verified; India delays implementation

name: Antwerp Diamond District
owner: Antwerp World Diamond Centre (AWDC) — trade body for ~1,700 companies
production: ~$30B annual rough diamond trade; handles ~80% of world's rough diamonds by value
strategic_value: Historic center of global diamond trade; EU sanctions on Russian diamonds (Jan 2024) directly impact Antwerp; G7 provenance verification system being built here to track Russian stones
alert: Direct Russian rough diamond imports banned since Jan 2024; indirect imports (via 3rd countries) banned from Sep 2024; enforcement challenging

name: China Lab-Grown Diamond Industry
owner: Multiple firms — Henan Huanghe Whirlwind, Zhongnan Diamond, Ningbo Crysdiam
production: ~50-60% of global lab-grown diamonds; Henan province alone produces majority; capacity growing 30%/year
strategic_value: China's lab-grown diamond dominance threatens De Beers/Alrosa natural diamond model; prices crashed 40% in 2023-2024; could collapse African diamond economies dependent on natural stones
alert: Lab-grown prices crashing threatens Botswana, Angola, South Africa economies; De Beers exited lab-grown market in 2024

name: India Lab-Grown Diamond Sector
owner: Multiple firms — Greenlab Diamonds, Laxmi Diamond, CVD Equipment Corp licensees
production: ~25-30% of global lab-grown production; Surat factories pivoting from natural to lab-grown cutting
strategic_value: India positioning itself on both sides — processes 90% of natural diamonds AND growing share of lab-grown; hedging strategy as market shifts; PM Modi gifted lab-grown diamond to Jill Biden in 2023

name: Ghana Gold Mining Sector
owner: Multiple: Newmont (Ahafo, Akyem), Gold Fields (Tarkwa, Damang), AngloGold Ashanti (Obuasi), artisanal miners (galamsey)
production: ~4.0 Moz/year — Africa's largest gold producer, world's 6th largest
strategic_value: Surpassed South Africa as Africa's top gold producer in 2019. Western mining companies dominate large-scale operations. Illegal artisanal mining (galamsey) destroying water sources and forests. Government crackdown ongoing.
alert: Galamsey crisis: illegal Chinese-financed artisanal mining destroying cocoa farmland and rivers. Government deployed military to mining sites.

name: Australia Gold Mining Sector
owner: Multiple: Newmont (Boddington, Tanami), Northern Star (Kalgoorlie Super Pit), Evolution Mining, Gold Road Resources
production: ~10.6 Moz/year — world's 2nd largest gold producer after China
strategic_value: Major Western-aligned gold supply source. AUKUS member. Kalgoorlie Super Pit is one of world's largest open-pit gold mines. Australian gold processed domestically — no Chinese supply chain dependency.
